outcome: No result found that advances the Bost conjecture (the l1-Banach algebra analogue of the Baum-Connes assembly map, as a case of the Farrell-Jones framework) since 26 January 2024; it remains open in general, with the pre-2024 known cases (word-hyperbolic groups, groups acting on trees, open subgroups) unchanged.
summary: The Bost conjecture in this bullet is the l1(G)-Banach-algebra analogue of the Baum-Connes assembly map (that the assembly map A_FIN^{l1}: H_n^G(E_FIN(G); K_{l1}^top) -> K_n(l1(G)) is an isomorphism), treated as a special/related case within the Farrell-Jones isomorphism-conjecture framework. I searched directly for the Bost conjecture by name (plain, with 'Farrell-Jones', with 'Baum-Connes', with 'Banach algebra', in French as 'conjecture de Bost', and restricted to arXiv and to 2024/2025/2026), and separately searched adjacent literature (Baum-Connes for relatively hyperbolic groups, coarse Baum-Connes, Banach KK-theory) for any paper that also addresses the Bost conjecture. Every hit is either (a) pre-2024 background (the 2009 Bost-conjecture-for-open-subgroups/tree-actions paper, the 2013 'Bost conjecture and proper Banach algebras' paper), (b) a same-name coincidence — an entirely different 'Bost conjecture' (J.-B. Bost's 1997 conjecture that tensor products of semistable Hermitian/Arakelov lattices are semistable, which is unrelated to the Farrell-Jones framework and not the subject of this bullet), or (c) work on the neighboring but distinct Baum-Connes conjecture itself (e.g. arXiv:2512.21169, December 2025, 'Strong bolicity and the Baum-Connes conjecture for relatively hyperbolic groups') that does not mention or extend the Bost conjecture specifically. I fetched the 2025 Lück survey 'Survey on the Farrell-Jones Conjecture' (arXiv:2507.11337, published in the Bulletin of the AMS 2026) directly and it contains no mention of the Bost conjecture at all, suggesting it has not been a locus of recent activity even in the most current comprehensive survey of the surrounding conjecture family. I also fetched the Farrell-Jones conjecture's current Wikipedia article, which describes the Bost conjecture but states no proof or new-case result. No AI system appears anywhere in this search. I agree with the triage's 'none' verdict and its reasoning, and did not find anything it missed.
competing_reading: It is possible a paper proves the Bost conjecture for some further class of groups (e.g. some new class of non-positively-curved or acylindrically hyperbolic groups) without using the words 'Bost conjecture' prominently in its abstract or title, instead phrasing it purely in terms of the l1-assembly-map or K-theory of l1(G) — such a paper could be missed by name-based search. I did not find any such paper in the Baum-Connes/Banach K-theory literature I surveyed, but I cannot rule out its existence with certainty.
what_would_settle_it: A full-text search of arXiv's math.KT and math.OA listings for 2024-2026 for the phrase 'l1(G)' or 'K_*(l1(G))' combined with 'assembly map' or 'isomorphism conjecture', which would catch a paper that proves new Bost-conjecture cases without naming Bost explicitly; or a citation-graph check (Google Scholar 'cited by') on the two canonical Bost-conjecture papers (Lafforgue's original result, and the 2009/2013 papers found here) restricted to 2024 onward.
